h: Curry, Culture and a Model Village
p: Bradford had a big moment as UK City of Culture in 2025, and it's a city that's always had more to offer than its reputation suggests. The Broadway shopping centre puts Flip Out right in the middle of things, so you can easily bolt on a meal and a bit of exploring.

Speaking of meals, Bradford has a proud reputation for curry and has been crowned the UK's Curry Capital more than once. After a sweaty session on the trampolines, a family curry is a very Bradford way to round off the day.

Just outside the city, Saltaire is a must-see. It's a Victorian model village built by mill owner Sir Titus Salt for his workers, and it's now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Salts Mill houses a big collection of art by Bradford-born David Hockney, along with shops and a café, and Roberts Park across the river is lovely for a stroll.
Bradford Industrial Museum, at Moorside Mills, is another good one for families, with working machinery and a peek into how the city's wool trade worked.

Fancy heading into the hills? Haworth, the home of the Brontë sisters, is a short drive away. The Brontë Parsonage Museum is where they lived and wrote, and the steep cobbled Main Street is full of tearooms. The Keighley and Worth Valley Railway also runs heritage trains through the area.
In the city centre itself, the Little Germany quarter has grand Victorian warehouses that are worth a wander, especially for anyone who likes old architecture.
